info.name: MediQueue - Day 6 No-Show Tracker Tests
info.description: Verifies the Day 6 sliding-window no-show tracker end to end: two doctors with identical avgConsultationTime, one clean and one with an 80% no-show history, compared on the GET /appointments/{id}/queue-status endpoint. Run the whole collection top to bottom with Collection Runner (Setup -> Baseline Doctor A -> Build Doctor B History -> Fresh Queue Test -> Negative Checks). Setup registers each account, then explicitly calls POST /api/auth/login for it and uses the login-issued token for every request that follows - so this suite exercises the real two-step auth flow (and gives /login actual test coverage) rather than relying on the token /register happens to also return. All variables are collection-scoped and populated automatically by each request's test script - no manual copy-pasting of tokens or IDs required. Re-runnable: emails are randomized per run and pinned to a variable at registration time so the matching Login request can find the same account.

request.description: SecurityConfig has no permitAll rule for this path - everything not under /api/auth/**, /error, or /api/health requires anyRequest().authenticated(). The controller method itself has no @PreAuthorize, so any authenticated role works here, but a token is mandatory. Without one this comes back 403 (not 401 - this app never configures an AuthenticationEntryPoint, so Spring Security's fallback Http403ForbiddenEntryPoint is what you get for missing/invalid auth everywhere, not just for real role failures).

item.name: 5. Negative Checks
Queue Status - rejected for non-owning patient (expect 400)

request.description: Patient Two tries to read Patient One's appointment. This comes back 400, not 403, because the ownership check is a plain RuntimeException caught by GlobalExceptionHandler's generic handler - it's an application-level check, not a Spring Security @PreAuthorize failure. Compare against the next request, which IS a @PreAuthorize failure and does return 403.

@PreAuthorize("hasAnyRole('DOCTOR','ADMIN')") rejects this, but NOT via a servlet filter - method security is AOP-based, so the AccessDeniedException it throws happens inside normal Spring MVC dispatch and gets caught by GlobalExceptionHandler's catch-all RuntimeException handler, same as the ownership check above. Both come back 400 here. A 403 would only happen if the request had no valid authentication at all (the missing-token case tested elsewhere in this collection), which is handled at the filter level, before MVC dispatch, and never reaches GlobalExceptionHandler.
